2027-01-06.title: Denho · The Baptism of our Lord
readings: You are my Son, the Beloved
Rebekah gives water at the well
The river flowing from the Temple
Draw water from the wells of salvation
Baptised in the name of the Lord Jesus
The water of rebirth and renewal
The Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan
2027-01-06.alt: Denho, the Baptism of our Lord: a day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. In many parishes the waters are solemnly blessed.
2027-01-06.verse: This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.
theo: Denho means “rising” or “manifestation”. At the Jordan the hidden Child of Bethlehem is revealed to the world. When Jesus comes up from the water, “the heavens were opened to him and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. And a voice from heaven said, ‘This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.’” For the first time the whole Holy Trinity is manifested: the Father speaks, the Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends.

John protests: “I need to be baptized by you.” Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; for it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness.” The sinless One goes down into the waters of repentance with sinners. He does not need to be cleansed; he cleanses the waters. The Fathers say that by his Baptism Christ sanctified the waters for our Baptism.

The Old Testament readings are full of water: Rebekah drawing water for a stranger and his camels; water filling the dry valley; Ezekiel's river flowing from the Temple, where “everything will live where the river goes”; Isaiah's promise: “With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” All these streams flow into the Jordan, and from the Jordan into our baptismal font.

St Paul tells Titus: “the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all”, and God saved us “through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit”. Denho is our feast too. In Baptism the Father said to each of us, “You are my beloved child”, and the Spirit came to dwell in us. Today we renew that grace.
conn: Father, Son and Holy Spirit appear together at the Jordan, as the Son later sends the apostles to baptise “in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19).
The dove over the waters recalls the Spirit hovering over the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2) and the dove of the flood (Genesis 8:11): a new creation begins.
Ezekiel's river (47:1–12) flows again in Revelation 22:1, “the river of the water of life… flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb”.
Baptism in the name of Jesus.
In Acts 19 Paul baptises disciples who knew only John's baptism, and the Holy Spirit comes upon them: Christian Baptism gives the Spirit.
altar: The Spirit who descended on Jesus at the Jordan descends on the bread and wine at every Holy Qurbono. The water mixed with the wine in the chalice recalls our Baptism and our union with Christ.
outline: Recall our own baptism day: who brought us, who were our godparents?
The Trinity at the Jordan: the Father's voice, the Son, the Spirit.
The sinless One goes down among sinners; he cleanses the waters for us.
Rebekah, Ezekiel, Isaiah: water as God's gift of life.
Baptism makes us children of God. Renew the baptismal promises.
“In Christ, I too am the Father's beloved child.”
live: Find out the date of your Baptism and keep it each year with a prayer of thanks.
Take home the blessed water of Denho; bless yourself and your children every night.
Pray the Creed slowly today as the renewal of your baptismal faith.
fathers: “Christ is baptised: let us go down with him, that we may also rise with him.” He comes to sanctify the Jordan for our sake (Oration 39, On the Holy Lights).
“Come down, my brothers, put on from the waters the Holy Spirit.” In his Hymns on the Epiphany he sings of the Lord who went down into the river and made the waters a womb of new birth.
magis: The baptism of Jesus is his acceptance of his mission as the Suffering Servant; the Spirit and the Father's voice reveal him. Through Baptism the Christian is sacramentally assimilated to Jesus.
The Lord's baptism and his Passover are the sources of Christian Baptism.
Baptism is the gateway to life in the Spirit; by it we are freed from sin and reborn as children of God.
saints: 7 Jan: Exaltation of St John the Baptist. 8 Jan: Mar Stephanos (St Stephen), the first martyr.
2027-01-06.prayer: Eternal Father, at the Jordan you revealed your beloved Son and sent your Holy Spirit upon him. Renew in us the grace of our Baptism, make us live as your beloved children, and let the river of your life flow through our homes and our Church. Amen.

quick: Denho: at the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed.
Christ, who has no sin, sanctifies the waters for our Baptism.
In Baptism the Father calls each of us “my beloved child”.
2027-01-06.action: Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it today.
2027-01-06.question: Do I live as the Father's beloved child?
2027-01-06.special: Denho, the Baptism of our Lord: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: In old Kerala Christian homes the date of Baptism was written inside the family Bible, beside the date of birth. Many grandparents knew it better than their birthday. Denho reminds us that the second birth matters even more than the first.

family.explain: Jesus was baptised by John in the river Jordan. Heaven opened, the Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and the Father said: “This is my beloved Son.” At our Baptism God said the same about us!
family.intention: We thank God for our Baptism and pray for our godparents.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the day each of us was baptised, and who our godparents are?”

kidsaint: He lived in the desert, called people to change their hearts, and had the joy of baptising Jesus. He said: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” Lesson: point others to Jesus, not to yourself.
term: Syriac for “rising” or “dawn”: the manifestation of Christ at his Baptism in the Jordan, 6 January. In the Malankara tradition the waters are solemnly blessed on this feast, and the faithful take the blessed water home.
termMore: From the early centuries the Eastern Churches celebrated on 6 January the manifestation of Christ, above all his Baptism. The season of Denho continues until the Great Fast.

pm.open: Father, at the Jordan you revealed your beloved Son and the Spirit descended upon him. Renew in us the grace of our Baptism. Amen.
share: This is my Son, the Beloved (Matthew 3:17). Do I live as a beloved child of God?
Let it be so now (Matthew 3:15). Where must I humbly accept God's way?
The river flowing from the temple brings life wherever it goes (Ezekiel 47:9). Where can I bring life this week?
interc: For all the baptized, that they may live as children of God.
For catechumens and those preparing for Baptism.
For godparents and parents, that they may hand on the faith.
For clean water and those who lack it.
For our group, that we may remember our Baptism with gratitude.
pm.close: Father, you made us your children in Baptism. Keep us faithful to the grace we received in the water and the Spirit. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Denho, the feast of the manifestation of the Lord. The Child of Bethlehem, hidden for thirty years in Nazareth, comes to the Jordan and is revealed to the world. When he comes up out of the water, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice says: “This is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased.”

John did not want to baptise him: “I need to be baptised by you!” But Jesus went down into the water with sinners. Why? He had no sin to wash away. The Fathers answer: he went down to make the waters holy for us. The Jordan became the source of every baptismal font in the world.

Our Old Testament readings are full of water: Rebekah at the well, a river flowing from the Temple bringing life wherever it goes, Isaiah's joyful promise: “With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” In our Baptism we drank from those wells. And the same voice spoke over each of us: “You are my beloved child.”

Today, as the waters are blessed, let us renew our baptismal promises with faith. Take the blessed water home; bless your children with it each night. Find out the date of your Baptism and thank God for it every year. Live as beloved children of the Father, filled with the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember the day Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. When he came out of the water, heaven opened!
The Holy Spirit came down like a white dove, and God the Father said: “This is my beloved Son!” Father, Son and Holy Spirit, all together.
When you were baptised, God said: “You are my beloved child!” Do you know your baptism day? Ask your parents tonight! Let's say: “I am God's beloved child!”

intro: Isaiah prayed: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down.” At the Jordan the prayer is answered.

points.apply: Thank God for coming close to you.
Make the sign of the cross slowly and with faith today.

sub: He sanctifies the water for us.
points.apply: Bless yourself with holy water when you enter church.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opens and the Trinity is revealed.
In Baptism heaven opened for us too.
opts.resolve: I will make the sign of the cross with faith, remembering that heaven opened at my Baptism.
homily: Dear friends, long ago Isaiah cried out: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down (Isaiah 64:1). Israel longed for God to come close. At the Jordan the prayer is answered: as Jesus came up from the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him (Mark 1:10).

This is the great manifestation of the Trinity. The Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends, and the Father's voice says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:17). Every time we make the sign of the cross, we confess what was revealed at the Jordan.
Jesus did not need to be cleansed. The Fathers said: he went into the water not to be made holy by it, but to make the waters holy for us. From that day, water became the doorway into God's life.

Paul says: he saved us through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). What happened at the Jordan happened to us at the font. Heaven opened over us; the Father called us his children.
Today let us thank God for our Baptism, make the sign of the cross with faith, and come to the Holy Qurbono as children of an open heaven. Amen.

intro: Most of us were baptised as infants and remember nothing. Today the Church asks us to remember what God did.

points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it.
Live one day this week as if wearing your baptismal garment.

sub: The candle lit from the Easter flame.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises tonight: I reject sin; I believe.

concl: Baptism is not only a past event but a present identity.
We live as children of God, clothed with Christ, walking in the light.
opts.resolve: This week I will find my Baptism date, thank my godparents, and renew my baptismal promises.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, most of us were baptised as infants. We do not remember the water, the oil or the candle. Today, as we celebrate the Lord's own baptism, the Church invites us to remember what God did to us.

Paul asks: do you not know that all of us who have been baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death? We were buried with him by baptism, so that we too might walk in newness of life (Romans 6:3–4). The font is both a tomb and a womb.

He also says: as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:27). That is why we received a white garment. We are called to wear Christ every day, at home, at work, in our words.

At Baptism a candle was lit for us, and our godparents spoke promises on our behalf: to reject sin and to believe. Now that we are grown, those promises are ours to keep. Once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light (Ephesians 5:8).
So let us find the date of our Baptism, thank our godparents, and tonight renew our promises: I reject sin; I believe in God. Then come to the Holy Qurbono as children of the light. Amen.

intro: Theme: “The heavens opened: the Son, the Spirit, the Father, and our Baptism.”
Denho means “dawning” or “manifestation”. At the Jordan Jesus is revealed as the beloved Son, the Spirit rests on him, and the Father speaks. Today we also remember our own Baptism.

points.h: The sinless One enters our waters
sub: John protests: “I need to be baptized by you.”
Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; it is proper for us to fulfil all righteousness”: he stands with sinners.
The Fathers say: he did not need the waters to make him holy; he made the waters holy for us.
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
But Jesus answered him, “Let it be so now; for it is proper for us in this way to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he consented.
points.apply: Thank God for the humility of Christ, who stands in line with sinners.

sub: The heavens are torn apart: God's distance is overcome.
The Spirit descends like a dove; the Father's voice declares the beloved Son.
Isaiah's servant, filled with the Spirit, is revealed: Jesus is the Christ, the Anointed.
q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.

And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross today slowly, thinking of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

points.h: Our Baptism: drawing water from the wells of salvation
sub: Isaiah promised joy from the wells of salvation.
In Baptism the same Spirit came upon us; in Chrismation we were sealed with holy Myron.
St Paul's disciples at Ephesus received the Spirit when hands were laid on them.
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
He saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it every year.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opened; at our Baptism heaven opened for us.
Let us live as beloved children of the Father, filled with the Spirit, following the Son.
2027-01-06.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises at home this week: reject sin and profess the Creed.
